title: Tamagoyaki Japanese Rolled Omelette

description: Tamagoyaki is a delightful Japanese rolled omelette, known for its subtly sweet or savory flavor and distinctive layered texture. It is a staple in Japanese breakfasts, bento boxes, and sushi platters, offering a comforting taste of traditional Japanese home cooking. Mastering its preparation is a rewarding experience for any culinary enthusiast.

adjust to taste for sweeter omelette

instructions.title: Prepare the Egg Mixture
instructions.text: Crack eggs into a bowl. Whisk gently until whites and yolks are just combined, being careful not to create too many air bubbles. In a separate small bowl, combine dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and salt. Stir until sugar and salt are dissolved. Add this dashi mixture to the eggs and whisk gently to combine. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any chalazae and ensure a smooth omelette. This step is crucial for a silky texture.

instructions.title: Heat the Tamagoyaki Pan
instructions.text: Place a rectangular tamagoyaki pan (or a small non-stick frying pan) over medium-low heat. Lightly grease the pan with a small amount of vegetable oil using a paper towel. Ensure the pan is evenly coated and not pooling with oil.

instructions.title: Pour the First Layer
instructions.text: Once the pan is hot, pour about one-quarter to one-fifth of the egg mixture into the pan, tilting it to form a thin, even layer that covers the bottom. Pop any large bubbles with a chopstick.

instructions.title: Roll the First Layer
instructions.text: As soon as the edges set and the top is mostly cooked but still slightly wet, use chopsticks or a spatula to gently roll the omelette from one end to the other. Push the rolled omelette to one side of the pan.

instructions.title: Cook Subsequent Layers
instructions.text: Lightly re-grease the empty part of the pan. Pour another portion of the egg mixture under and around the rolled omelette, lifting the rolled portion slightly so the new egg mixture flows underneath. Cook until the new layer is mostly set.

instructions.title: Continue Rolling
instructions.text: Once the new layer is cooked, roll the existing omelette over the fresh layer, continuing to form a thicker roll. Push the growing omelette back to the starting side of the pan. Repeat steps 5 and 6 until all the egg mixture is used, forming a multi-layered omelette.

instructions.title: Shape and Slice
instructions.text: Once all the egg mixture is used and the omelette is fully cooked, remove it from the pan and place it on a bamboo rolling mat (makisu) or a cutting board. Gently shape it into a neat rectangle using the mat or by pressing with a spatula. Let it cool for a few minutes before slicing into 1-inch thick pieces.

tips: For a perfectly smooth Tamagoyaki, always strain your egg mixture to remove any bits of chalazae and air bubbles.
Adjust the amount of sugar and mirin to your preference; some prefer a sweeter Tamagoyaki, while others like it more savory.
A rectangular tamagoyaki pan is ideal, but a small non-stick round pan can also be used by carefully shaping the omelette.
